title: Serverless was a big mistake... says Amazon
summary: Fireship on the Prime Video post: merging serverless step functions into one container cut cost 90% by removing serialization and network hops, but Netflix-scale fault tolerance and small-team serverless convenience still justify distribution.

assertions.quote: they saved 90 on their Amazon web services bill by switching from serverless microservices to an Old-Fashioned monolith architecture
if Netflix goes down for a few hours it'll cost them way more money and lost memberships
I can easily deploy my shitty JavaScript code without ever having to think about infrastructure I rarely even bust out of the free tier

verdicts.note: True for low, bursty traffic; costs and limits bite at sustained load, as the same video's Prime Video case shows.

assertions.quote: when it comes to Cloud architecture there are no Solutions only trade-offs
